issues.description: The problem statement requires Farm to initialize its internal ArrayList in a constructor with no arguments, and the template (Main.java) expects to instantiate Farm with new Farm(). However, the solution implements only a constructor with a single int parameter (public Farm(int initialCapacity)) and does not provide a no-argument constructor. This mismatch means code that uses new Farm() (as shown in the template's Main) or tests expecting a default constructor will fail to compile against the solution, and students following the problem instructions to implement a no-arg constructor would find the provided solution inconsistent.
issues.suggestedFix: Provide a no-argument constructor in Farm that initializes the animals list (e.g. public Farm() { this.animals = new ArrayList<>(); }). Alternatively, if an initial-capacity constructor is desired, also add a no-arg constructor that delegates to it so code and tests using new Farm() compile and match the problem specification.
